# Draft:Disability in the Republic of Ireland

Disability in the Republic of Ireland covers a wide range of conditions and experiences, impacting the lives of millions of people. Defined by the Disability Act 2005 as a "substantial restriction in the capacity of the person to carry on a profession, business or occupation in the State or to participate in social or cultural life in the State by reason of an enduring physical, sensory, mental health or intellectual impairment", it encompasses various aspects of life, including demographics, legislation, healthcare, employment, and culture. The Government of Ireland has The National Human Rights Strategy for Disabled People 2025-2030 plan to realise the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities.
Governance
Government policy that represents disabled people in the Republic of Ireland is handled by the Department of Children, Disability and Equality and the National Disability Authority.
Demographics
In the 2022 census, the Central Statistics Office recorded that 22% of the Republic of Ireland's population were disabled (1,109,557 people), 8% of the population (407,342) having experienced at least one long-lasting condition or "difficulty to a great extent or a lot" and 14% of the population (702,215) having experienced at least one long-lasting condition or "difficulty to some extent or a little"
